name: Richard Ivey Building
summary: Three-storey quadrangle flanked by low rough-stone pavilions, with tall dark-framed glass bays along Western Road and rows of narrower office windows on the south elevation.

evidence.note: Low roughly coursed stone wall with a recessed group of ground windows. Two-storey glazing has narrow dark vertical members and broad smooth end panels.
Upper glazing in a deep rectangular stone frame above the lawn.
South approach shows repeated tall single and grouped punched office windows over a more continuous ground-floor band.
Daylight photograph of the glazed projections, pale smooth returns, rough base and deep horizontal entrance overhang. Wall colour sampled from frame 34490888.
Ivey identifies a three-storey building around a central courtyard, built with local limestone, flagstone, rubble stone and copper.
Pedestrian entry by the Western Road and Brescia intersection.
City of London 2025 orthophoto. Open landscaped court, projecting flat-roofed pavilions, a dark L-shaped pitched roof, long strips of glazing, and rooftop plant on the southwest projection.
Inventory P50 13.37 m, P90 15.71 m, maximum 17.03 m. Outer stone pavilions sample around 5–6 m, southwest block near 9 m, office roof about 13–14 m and north/west roof rises to 16–17 m.
Richard Ivey drops from 16.8 m at the outer west range to 14.2 m near the courtyard along a constant-v lidar transect, and the north range also falls toward its courtyard terrace.

notes: Limestone end panels separate glazed upper bays. The exact frontage bay depths and the extent of the planted eastern roof remain approximate.
